drug_class: Opioid partial agonist / opioid antagonist combination (medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder)
purpose: This medication is used to treat opioid use disorder, helping people who are dependent on opioids like heroin or prescription painkillers. It reduces cravings and withdrawal symptoms so you can focus on your recovery. It is usually used as part of a full treatment program that includes counseling and support.
how_it_works: Buprenorphine is a partial opioid — it attaches to the same receptors in your brain that opioids do, but only partially activates them. This calms cravings and eases withdrawal without giving you a strong high. Naloxone is added as a safety component — if someone tries to inject the medication to misuse it, the naloxone will block the opioid effect and cause withdrawal, discouraging misuse.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include headache, nausea, constipation, sweating, trouble sleeping, and mouth numbness or pain where the film or tablet dissolves. Some people also feel tired or dizzy, especially when starting the medication.
warnings: Do not take this medication with alcohol, sleeping pills, benzodiazepines (like Xanax or Valium), or other sedatives — combining them can slow your breathing and be life-threatening. Never share this medication with others. It can cause serious harm or death in people who are not opioid-dependent, especially children. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, as this medication requires special management during pregnancy.
typical_dosing: This medication is usually placed under your tongue or between your cheek and gum and allowed to dissolve — do not swallow or chew it. Dosing is individualized, but most adults start with a low dose on the first day and gradually increase to a typical maintenance dose of 8mg/2mg to 24mg/6mg (buprenorphine/naloxone) per day, taken once daily. Your doctor will find the right dose that controls your cravings and withdrawal symptoms.
